av_event.what: A cocker spaniel jumps up onto the single bed with the sage-green duvet in the lower right corner of Hannah's frame, turns round once and lies down, staying partly visible for the rest of the call.

text:
A: Hiii! Hi, I'm Holly! Last one, yay!
B: Hi! I'm Hannah. How are you doing?
A: I'm good, thanks, how are you? Okay, someone just told me your dog's called Biscuit.
B: [laughs] Was that Karim? Yeah, he is. He's a cocker spaniel, though, not a cockapoo, so I feel a bit left out.
A: No, you're in the club. There's three of us. We should start a group chat. Biscuit mums.
B: Sorry, I love that. Mine rolled in something horrible on Dartmoor on Sunday, so he's not really a group chat dog at the moment.
A: Mine eats my trainers. Only the nice ones. So what do you do? You look like a teacher, in a good way.
B: [laughs] Nearly! I'm doing a PGCE in Exeter, primary. I'm on placement in a Year 1 class at the moment, so I'm a bit knackered.
A: Oh my god, five-year-olds. I'd be terrible. What's it like?
B: It's so full on, but they're hilarious. And I'm quite organised, so, erm, colour-coded lesson plans, laminating, all that. My mentor says I should take more risks.
A: I'm literally the opposite. I'm GM of a cocktail bar in Chelmsford and my assistant manager basically does all my paperwork. I'm good with people, rubbish with spreadsheets. Do you know what I mean?
B: Yeah, I'm good with spreadsheets. Sorry, that's a really boring thing to be proud of.
A: No! That's a superpower. If you ever want a job, I'm serious. [laughs]
B: [laughs] I do café shifts at a garden centre in the holidays, so I'd be okay with the coffee. Not the cocktails.
A: I'd teach you. Okay, I have to ask, I saw your noticeboard. Is that a Wicked ticket?
B: Yeah! I've seen it twice, once in London and once on tour at Plymouth. I'd go again tomorrow.
A: Stop. I go to a musical every birthday. Wicked's my favourite, I cried at Defying Gravity, like properly.
B: Everyone cries at Defying Gravity. My mum cried both times. We watch Strictly and Bake Off together every week as well, so it's basically our thing.
A: Aw, that's so nice. Do you live with them?
B: Yeah, I'm back at home for the PGCE. Which is nice, but sometimes I see friends who've moved out and got proper jobs and I'm like, I'm still in my old bedroom.
A: Honestly, don't rush it. We bought a house and now I'm skint every month. Your mum's cooking you dinner, that's the dream.
B: Her roast is the best thing in the world, to be fair. Are you from Chelmsford, then?
A: Born and raised. Okay, but going back to Wicked. Have you been to New York? Because that's where you need to see it next, on Broadway.
B: That's literally my dream trip! I've never been. I'm not really a big traveller, I'm very much Cornwall and Menorca, but New York for Broadway, I'd do that.
A: You have to go. Ryan would book it, I'd just turn up. I'm terrible at planning.
B: I'd plan it for you. I'd do a spreadsheet.
A: See, this is why we need each other! So when you're qualified, where do you want to be?
B: Devon, ideally Key Stage 1. Erm, close to home. I'm applying now, so kind of fingers crossed.
A: You'll walk it. Honestly, anyone with laminated lesson plans, they'd be mad not to
B: Sorry, I hope so! I'll tell
